question: What causes a model to stop producing tokens and end its response?

options.text: The app enforces a fixed number of words per reply
options.feedback: Apps can cap a reply, but that is not how a response normally ends. The model itself decides when it is done, using a token reserved for exactly that purpose.

options.text: Every token's probability drops too low for one to be chosen
options.feedback: The model always produces a full probability distribution over the vocabulary, so there is always a token to choose. Stopping is a positive choice the model makes, not a failure to find anything.

options.text: One of the tokens in the vocabulary means "stop," and the model chooses it
options.feedback: This is the end-of-sequence token, and picking it is a prediction like any other -- the model works out that it is finished the same way it works out any next word. That is why a reply can be one line or several paragraphs, depending only on the context.

options.text: The response is cut off once it reaches the length of the prompt
options.feedback: Prompt length and response length are unrelated. A short question can get a long answer and vice versa, because the model chooses the stopping point itself with a dedicated token.
